description:
## Why this ticket exists

Zero lifecycle scripts is a design pillar (npm 12 / pnpm 10 block dependency scripts by default; our install path needs none) — so there is no postinstall hook to do setup. **Bare `spendbar` IS the first-run wizard** ("install it, run it", per the plan's Onboarding section and the approved-plan handover). This ticket ships that wizard plus the two trust-critical companions, `doctor` and `uninstall`. Blocked by T-015 because the wizard installs, and doctor diagnoses, the launcher/LaunchAgent/attach machinery that T-015 finalizes.

## Scope (in)

- **First-run wizard** (bare `spendbar`, re-runnable as `spendbar setup`): instant today-$ (~1–2 s — **conditional on the clone-capable path**; non-APFS fallback is unproven and unbenchmarked, per plan) → note that background indexing is handed to the durable service that survives the CLI's exit → **auto-detected consent prompts**: (a) service + login item, (b) `claude mcp add` if `claude` is on PATH, (c) `codex mcp add` if `~/.codex` exists. `--yes` accepts for scripters.
- **MCP registration goes through the launcher** (explicit `mcp` mode or validated absolute paths) — never a PATH-dependent shebang bin, because GUI-launched clients don't have the package manager's PATH (round-2 finding).
- **`doctor`**: launcher/plist health, node path validity, snapshot freshness, MCP registration health verified **against real client launches**, permission-denied explanations — **every finding prints its fix**.
- **`uninstall`**: ownership fingerprints recorded at install time; entries in external files (Claude/Codex MCP config, plists, login items) removed **only on fingerprint match**; prompt on divergence; `--purge-data` is a separate flag **with a dry-run mode**.
- **Permissions phrasing (round-2, exact stance)**: claim only that no permission prompts are *expected* for default `~/.claude` / `~/.codex` paths on the tested macOS matrix — NOT an unconditional "zero TCC" guarantee; doctor detects and explains permission-denied.
- **Interim behavior preserved**: in v0.1–0.2 bare `spendbar` prints MCP registration one-liners (already true); the wizard supersedes that in v0.3.

## Scope (out)

- The passive update line — designed in the Onboarding section but phased into **v0.4** by the plan's phase table. The standing rule that applies *now*: **never self-mutating updates** — the wizard must never update or modify the installation itself.
- Settings UI (v0.4); brew distribution (v0.5); launcher/LaunchAgent mechanics themselves (T-011/T-015).

## Approach notes & constraints

- Non-darwin platforms: the service/login-item prompts are darwin-only; elsewhere the plan's rule is clear capability messages, with the CLI/MCP portions still usable.
- Declining prompts must be a first-class path — the wizard's detection ("claude on PATH", "~/.codex exists") drives which prompts even appear.
- `uninstall` edits other tools' config files; that is the highest-blast-radius surface here — the fingerprint-match rule exists precisely so spendbar never deletes an entry it cannot prove it wrote.
- Standing constraints: no real transcript data or personal paths in fixtures; package.json carries no author field.

## Acceptance criteria
1. On a clean darwin user with a fresh install, bare `spendbar` prints today-$ and states that indexing was handed to the durable service; on the clone-capable path the warm run completes in ~1–2 s (recorded-baseline comparison, not a hard CI gate, per quality rulings).
2. Prompt detection verified in both directions: no `claude` on PATH ⇒ no Claude MCP prompt; no `~/.codex` ⇒ no Codex prompt; both present ⇒ both prompts appear.
3. Declining every prompt leaves the system untouched — Claude/Codex config files, plists, and login items are byte-identical before/after (diffed in the test).
4. `spendbar --yes` (or wizard-equivalent) completes unattended with exit 0 and performs all consented installs; a second `spendbar setup` run on a healthy install is idempotent (no changes).
5. MCP entries written by the wizard reference the launcher or validated absolute paths — never a shebang bin — verified both by inspecting the written client config and by a real GUI-launched Claude Code and Codex session successfully starting the spendbar MCP server.
6. `doctor` scenario tests each produce a specific finding WITH a printed fix: healthy install (all green), broken recorded node path (nvm version removed), stale snapshot, service owned by a foreign installation, mangled/missing MCP registration, permission-denied on ~/.claude or ~/.codex.
7. `uninstall` removes only fingerprint-matched external entries; a hand-edited (divergent) entry triggers a prompt and is never silently removed; `--purge-data --dry-run` prints exactly what would be deleted and deletes nothing; `--purge-data` then removes it and is verified.
8. No help text or doc claims an unconditional zero-permission-prompt guarantee; the wording matches the round-2 'expected on the tested matrix' phrasing.
9. Wizard/doctor/uninstall fixtures contain no real transcript data or personal paths.

## Risks
uninstall mutates external client configs — a fingerprint or matching bug can corrupt a user's Claude/Codex setup, which is the fastest way to lose the trust the product is positioned on. The ~1–2 s instant-$ promise is conditional on APFS clone support; the fallback path is unbenchmarked, so first-run UX on non-clone volumes is unknown. Detection heuristics (PATH, ~/.codex) can false-positive in odd environments. TCC behavior on MDM-managed Macs is outside the tested matrix and only mitigated by doctor's explanations.

## Open questions (owner decisions)
1. Should a blanket `--yes` also authorize writing MCP registrations into both clients' configs, or is modifying other tools' configs invasive enough to warrant separate opt-in flags for scripted installs?
title: Onboarding: bare-spendbar wizard, doctor, ownership-fingerprinted uninstall
